scopeDecisions.decision: Only local registered Functions targets can be rewritten. No Cloud Run lookup or live Functions fallback is allowed. Missing local targets remain unverified and are not an approved production equivalence.

Production is observed only through disposable preview channels (24 hour TTL) of the default site of the Identity Platform sandbox, one channel per site version, through the Hosting REST API. The live channel is never released to and the firebase CLI is not used, so the project's authorized domains are not written. A preview channel is not the live channel: a claim is limited to what a preview channel serves.

Function and Cloud Run rewrites are out of scope for this parent (owner ledger 2435). They are recorded as NOT_COMPARED with the official-emulator comparison as their only evidence. The REST API carries a file manifest, so the deploy-time `ignore` rule is not observable in production.

limitations: Observations come from preview channels only; the live channel is never touched.
Edge-set headers (date, age, via, x-cache*, x-served-by, x-timer, server, alt-svc) are recorded and never compared; any other header that is neither compared nor volatile must be named by the review.
The reserved initialization bodies keep byte count, line count and, for JSON, key order with value types and byte lengths; no value is retained.
ETag and Last-Modified are compared by form, not by value.
The redirect `type` default of the CLI is not observable through the REST API, which requires a status code.

The strict profile matches the recorded cases under productionExact. Under the default profile two development defaults differ from production on purpose (hosting.cacheControl "none": no default Cache-Control; hosting.clientCountry "honoured": X-Country-Code and the country cookie select i18n content); productionExact restores production for both (owner policy 1396/1403, coordinator ruling 23). A request outside the corpus is answered by the same rules, not by an observation.

Known differences (known-differences.json for the parent corpus, followup-known-differences.json for the follow-up corpus): Brotli encoding (KD-COMPRESSION and KD-BROTLI: production answers br to a request whose Accept-Encoding holds the text br; strict has no Brotli encoder and answers gzip when the header also holds gzip and identity when it does not), the length of a gzip body of a file of 100 to 1,500 bytes (KD-GZIP-LENGTH, coordinator ruling 27: 1 to 5 bytes longer in strict; the judge excuses it only when both answers are gzip, their decoded digests are equal and their content-lengths differ by at most 8 bytes, any other difference on those rows is a MISMATCH), the body of production's default 404 page and of the hosted /__/auth/handler page (KD-DEFAULT-404-BODY, KD-AUTH-HANDLER-PAGE: their bytes are not shipped, owner decision of 2026-11-11, so strict answers with pages written for fireemu; status, content type, Cache-Control and Vary are production's and are compared), the hosted SDK files (KD-SDK-FILES), the init.json layout beyond apiKey and projectId and the init.json and init.js lengths (KD-INIT-KEYS), and the host of the Location of a 302 for a path with dot segments (KD-SAFETY-ORIGIN-REDIRECT: production names an internal origin host that changes from request to request, strict names the host the request came to; the path of the Location is compared, rulings 17 and 21). Strict-transport-security, x-robots-tag and the SDK-row headers are excluded as edge-set. 18 of the 201 rows of each parent strict comparison and 42 of the 78 rows of each follow-up strict comparison carry a known difference and are counted as KNOWN_DIFFERENCE, not MATCH.

Gzip (rows v01.gz-*, v14.*, v15.*): strict looks for the text gzip in Accept-Encoding as a case-sensitive substring, as production does (x-gzip and gzip;q=0 get gzip; GZIP, *, deflate and identity do not, and every Accept-Encoding line counts); it compresses any content type when the gzip body is smaller than the file (production left files of 1 and 10 bytes alone and compressed files of 100 bytes and more; what it does from 11 to 99 bytes is not recorded, and `smaller than the file` is the reading used) from 1 byte to 32 MiB (an empty file and a larger one are answered as identity; the 32 MiB limit is strict's own, the whole answer being built in memory), with the file's own ETag and, for a Range, the range of the compressed body (206 with Content-Encoding: gzip, 416 when the range starts past it). A file with no known content type is text/html; charset=UTF-8 once compressed (rows v15.type-noext and -unknownext; its type uncompressed at this size is not recorded, v01 recorded text/plain for two bytes) and a .br file is application/octet-stream. A Content-Encoding header that a headers rule sets is not served: production ignored br, gzip and identity rules on four files (rows v14.*), so a precompressed file is sent as it is only because compressing it again does not make it smaller. The gzip header is the ten bytes production sent; the deflate stream of strict (miniz_oxide through flate2) is 1 to 5 bytes longer for files of 100 to 1,500 bytes (KD-GZIP-LENGTH, ruling 27, bounded at 8 bytes by the judge) and the same length at 2,048 and 4,500 bytes. Not recorded: other ranges over a compressed body and If-Range. Inferred, not recorded: a range that starts past the gzip length but inside the file answers 416 with `bytes */<gzip length>` and no Content-Encoding (the length of the compressed body, as the one recorded 416 over a compressed body suggests), and a range past the file answers the identity 416 with `bytes */<file length>`; production was not asked either.

Not compared: the body of init.js in the production-vs-local comparison (only init.json has a layout compared), and the bodies of the default 404 page and the hosted auth handler page (21,376 and 462 bytes, recorded as lengths and digests only: the published recordings do not hold them, owner decision of 2026-11-11).

Observed (rows v12.*, v13.*, v01.redirect-capture-*): a redirect whose source has a digit in a :name (/capture/:id/:id2, /p/:a1, /s/:a1/x, /t/:a1/:a2) matches nothing in production, neither the literal paths nor any other path tried, so strict never matches such a rule; a repeated name (/q/:id/:id) matches and the last value wins. How production reads other characters in a name (a hyphen, a literal after a name) is not recorded.

Dot segments (rows v01.safety-*, v11.dot-*, v11.backslash-*): production redirects a request with a dot segment to the normalized path (RFC 3986: empty segments stay, a path that ends in a dot segment ends in a slash as /a/b/.. gives /a/, an escaped dot is a dot), reads a raw backslash as a slash before it looks for dot segments (/.\\b gives /b, /a/./\\evil.example gives /a//evil.example, /./\\evil gives //evil), writes the hex digits of an escape that stays in upper case (%5c gives %5C; only that escape was seen) and answers a path with a backslash and no dot segment as any other path (404). The Location is absolute on an internal host, which strict replaces by the host the request came to, so a path that starts with // names no other host. The Host that goes in front of the path must be plain (letters, digits, dots, hyphens, a port, brackets): a Host with a slash, a backslash, an @, a ? or #, a space or an escape is refused with a 400, so the Location cannot name another origin.

Strict answers that no recording covers: 416 with Content-Range: bytes */N for an unsatisfiable range; a multi-range request answered whole; Range on HEAD answering 206 with the part's length and no body; If-Modified-Since on HEAD; OPTIONS on a path that is not a file (answered as any request); a path with dot segments and a control character or a space, which is not redirected (the recorder cannot send such a target); the query string of a dot-segment redirect, which is appended as sent; and the hosted /__/auth/ pages other than /__/auth/handler.

followUps: Optional probes, not needed for the claim: the gzip decision for files of 11 to 99 bytes (between the recorded 10 and 100), the content type of a text file with an unknown extension without compression, the upper-case rule for escapes other than %5c in a dot-segment redirect, other ranges and If-Range over a compressed body (including the two inferred 416 answers: a range past the gzip length but inside the file, and a range past the file), and the other pages under /__/auth/ (iframe, handler.js).
Brotli stays a declared difference (KD-COMPRESSION, KD-BROTLI); adding an encoder is a separate decision (owner ledger 2458 approved flate2 for gzip only).
